newsitem.title: USA: Oakland, Calif., readies $435 mln pension bonds.
newsitem.headline: Oakland, Calif., readies $435 mln pension bonds.

text.p: Oakland, Calif., plans to come to market with a $435 million pension obligation bond issue later this week amidst growing concerns about the city's financial obligations under a struggling 1995 stadium deal.

The taxable pension bonds, narrowly approved by the city council last week, are scheduled to be sold on a negotiated basis through a syndicate led by PaineWebber Inc. Grigsby & Associates is one of seven co-managers.
"We are planning to come to market on Thursday," said Janice Mazyck, Oakland's treasury manager. She said, however, market conditions for the pension bonds had to be just right.
"Certain market conditions must be present so that our savings target is met," Mazyck said of the deal, which has been in the works for about one year.
Standard & Poor's Corp has assigned an A-plus underlying rating to most of the bonds, which were rated single-A by Fitch Investors Service Inc.
But the bond issue comes at a difficult time for the city.

Last week, S&P revised its ratings outlook for Oakland to negative from stable, citing the city's troubled $200 million stadium bond issue for the Oakland Raiders, and the loss of revenue flexibility under California's Proposition 218.
Proposition 218, which was approved by voters last November, strengthened existing law to require that all new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval.

Stadium revenues are supposed to repay the bonds, but personal seat license sales for the National Football League Raiders have lagged projections. As a result, the city may have to use general funds to cover part of the debt service.

Proponents of the city's new pension obligation bond deal say the financing would save the city as much as $17 million over the next few years to help cushion the financial impact of the Raiders deal.
Proceeds from the pension bond sale will be used to fund a portion of the city's unfunded liability to its police and fire retirement system.
